alt: A handwritten-style panel titled Problem with Fully Connected Networks. A 28 by 28 grayscale image has 784 pixels, so 100 neurons need 784 times 100 equals 78,400 weights. A 224 by 224 by 3 colour image has 150,528 values. Five problems are listed: too many parameters, high computational cost, spatial information lost, no local feature detection, and the same feature at different locations not handled efficiently.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A 3 by 3 filter with weights w11 to w33 is applied at one place on a grid, then moved to the next place, and again. The note says same filter plus different locations equals weight sharing, which gives fewer parameters.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A table comparing a fully connected network with a CNN on six aspects: connection, weights, parameters, spatial information, computation and feature detection. The CNN uses local connections, reuses the same filter weights, has far fewer parameters, keeps spatial structure, is more efficient and detects a feature anywhere.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: Four boxes joined by arrows under the title What does CNN learn: early layers learn edges, middle layers learn curves, deeper layers learn parts, and the final layers recognize the complete object, shown as an apple.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A 3 by 3 input with numbers 1 to 9 and a 2 by 2 kernel with 1 0 0 1. The kernel on the top-left corner gives 1 plus 0 plus 0 plus 5 equals 6. The kernel then slides to the other three positions and the four results form the 2 by 2 feature map 6, 8, 12, 14.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A 3 by 3 feature map with values 2 1 0, 5 8 1, 0 4 2. A note says the numbers show the strength of the filter's response: a high value such as 8 means the feature is strongly present, a low value such as 0 means it is weak or not detected.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A 3 by 3 filter on a 5 by 5 grid of numbers 1 to 25 with stride 2. The filter starts at the top-left, jumps 2 pixels right, then 2 pixels down, then 2 right again, so only 4 positions are used.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A 3 by 3 input with a 2 by 2 filter, stride 2 and padding 0. The formula gives 1.5, so the output is 1 by 1. Only the first position is complete; the next positions would go outside the image, so they are not used.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: An original 3 by 3 grid of numbers 1 to 9 becomes a 5 by 5 grid after padding with one layer of zeros all around the border.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: Convolution on an RGB image at one position. The red, green and blue 3 by 3 regions are each multiplied with their own 3 by 3 filter, giving 10, 20 and 15. Adding the bias 2 gives 10 plus 20 plus 15 plus 2 equals 47, one value of the feature map.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: Trainable parameters of a convolution layer. One 3 by 3 by 3 filter has 27 weights plus 1 bias, so 28 parameters; 2 filters give 56. The general formula is (F times F times Din plus 1) times K.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A 4 by 4 feature map split into four 2 by 2 coloured blocks. Max pooling with a 2 by 2 filter and stride 2 keeps the largest value of each block, giving the 2 by 2 output 4, 8, 6, 9.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: The same 4 by 4 feature map pooled with a 2 by 2 filter and stride 2 by taking the average of each block, giving the 2 by 2 output 2.75, 4.5, 5, 5.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: The first half of a basic CNN: an RGB input of 32 by 32 by 3, convolution plus ReLU giving feature maps of 28 by 28 by 32, max pooling giving 14 by 14 by 32, a second convolution plus ReLU giving 10 by 10 by 64, and max pooling giving 5 by 5 by 64.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: The second half of a basic CNN: a flatten step makes a 1D vector of 1600 values, a fully connected layer of 128 neurons combines the features, softmax gives probabilities Cat 0.10, Dog 0.80, Horse 0.10 that sum to 1, and the predicted class is Dog because it has the highest probability.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A CNN pipeline: input volume 32 by 32 by 1, convolution with ReLU giving 28 by 28 by 3, max pooling with stride 2 giving 14 by 14 by 3, a flatten layer of 588 values, a fully connected layer with ReLU of 20 values, and a softmax layer with 5 output classes.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: A small image of a digit as a grid of 1 and minus 1 values is convolved with a 3 by 3 loopy-pattern filter to give a feature map with positive and negative values. ReLU turns every negative value into 0, and max pooling then keeps the largest value of each 2 by 2 block.
author: Deep Learning faculty
